competences: The learner identify durations in source sentences.
The learner use for correctly to state duration.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and uses correctly: for, duration, hours, years, present perfect.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify durations in source sentences.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to use for correctly to state duration.
priorKnowledge: Learners have compared since with for and can identify starting times.
materials: Duration cards showing four hours, two years and five hours

steps.content: Learners have compared since with for and can identify starting times. Key words: for, duration, hours, years, present perfect
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays duration cards showing four hours, two years and five hours and links the chart to the prior knowledge: Learners have compared since with for and can identify starting times. The teacher pronounces the lesson vocabulary, checks learners’ reading, and introduces using for.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall familiar words, read the displayed key words aloud, and explain what they already know about the topic.

source.quote: For is used when the length of time

steps.content: For expresses duration: For shows the length of time an action has lasted. An hour is a duration. Four hours is a duration. Two years is a duration. Five hours is a duration.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: For shows the length of time an action has lasted. An hour is a duration. Four hours is a duration. Two years is a duration. Five hours is a duration. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Complete the source sentence with for or since: They have played ___ four hours." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: For is used when the length of time

steps.content: Example 1: They have played for four hours. I have not seen my mother for two years. Joseph has sat there for five hours.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: They have played for four hours. I have not seen my mother for two years. Joseph has sat there for five hours. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Complete the source sentence with for or since: I have not seen my mother ___ two years." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: They have played for four hours

steps.stage: Development: Example 2: comparing for and since
steps.content: Example 2: comparing for and since: The baby has cried for an hour. The boy has been crying since 9:00 a.m. For introduces the duration. Since introduces the starting time.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: The baby has cried for an hour. The boy has been crying since 9:00 a.m. For introduces the duration. Since introduces the starting time. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Complete the source sentence with for or since: Joseph has sat there ___ five hours." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: The baby has cried for an hour

steps.content: Complete the source sentence with for or since: They have played ___ four hours. Complete the source sentence with for or since: I have not seen my mother ___ two years. Complete the source sentence with for or since: Joseph has sat there ___ five hours.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the following sourced text-based exercise: Complete the source sentence with for or since: They have played ___ four hours. Complete the source sentence with for or since: I have not seen my mother ___ two years. Complete the source sentence with for or since: Joseph has sat there ___ five hours. The teacher checks learners’ written answers for meaning, spelling and punctuation, using this key: for for for
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer individually in their books, use full sentences when required, read selected answers aloud, and correct spelling or punctuation after feedback.

source.quote: They have played for four hours

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher revisits these questions: Complete the source sentence with for or since: They have played ___ four hours. Complete the source sentence with for or since: I have not seen my mother ___ two years. Complete the source sentence with for or since: Joseph has sat there ___ five hours. The teacher checks whether learners have met the objectives, explains any remaining errors using the source text, and assigns the final exercise item for correction.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their answers with evidence from the text, read corrected sentences aloud, and note the final item for homework.
